name: Naqsh-e Jahan & the Bazaar
tagline: Live beside one of the world's great squares
description: The old core wraps around Naqsh-e Jahan Square, a vast Safavid maidan flanked by the Shah and Sheikh Lotfollah mosques, Ali Qapu palace and the covered Grand Bazaar. Traditional houses here have been converted into courtyard guesthouses with tiled pools and painted alcoves. Everything historic is within a fifteen-minute walk.
bestFor: Short stays where waking up beside the monuments is worth some tourist pricing.
pros: Every major sight within walking distance
Bazaar covers food, crafts and daily needs
cons: Tourist prices and persistent carpet sellers
Old buildings mean thin walls and weak wifi
Traffic and horns on the surrounding streets

name: Jolfa
tagline: Armenian quarter with Isfahan's cafe culture
description: New Jolfa is the Armenian district south of the Zayandeh River, founded under Shah Abbas I, centred on the frescoed Vank Cathedral and a small square of narrow lanes. It has by far the best cafe scene in the city, with roasteries, dessert houses and restaurants that stay busy late, plus a noticeably relaxed atmosphere.
bestFor: Remote workers who want cafes to sit and work in and a sociable evening scene.
pros: Best concentration of cafes with laptop seats
Walkable to Si-o-se Pol bridge and the river
cons: Rooms cost more than the rest of the city
Weekend evenings get crowded and loud

name: Chahar Bagh Abbasi
tagline: The grand tree-lined avenue through the middle
description: Chahar Bagh Abbasi is the Safavid promenade running north to south through central Isfahan, part of it pedestrianised, with plane trees, the Chehel Sotoun gardens, the Chahar Bagh madrasa and rows of shops, hotels and bakeries. Apartments on the side streets put you between the square, the river and the metro line.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to walk or take the metro rather than depend on taxis.
pros: Metro line runs directly beneath the avenue
Pedestrianised stretches good for evening walks
Central between the square, Jolfa and the river
cons: Traffic noise on the non-pedestrian sections
Some hotels here are dated and overpriced

name: Mardavij
tagline: Modern apartment blocks south of the river
description: Mardavij is a newer middle-class district south of the Zayandeh River, built around a broad boulevard of the same name with contemporary apartment towers, supermarkets, gyms and family restaurants. It has none of the historic architecture but the flats are modern, well-heated and much better value than a converted house in the old city.
bestFor: Monthly stays where a comfortable, well-connected flat matters more than atmosphere.
pros: Newer apartments with better heating and wiring
Quiet residential streets away from tour groups
Short taxi ride to Jolfa and the river bridges
cons: No historic character or old-town charm
Few cafes suited to working in
Boulevard traffic is heavy at rush hour

name: Kaveh & the North
tagline: Everyday local Isfahan at local prices
description: The northern districts along Kaveh Boulevard are working Isfahan: local bakeries, hardware shops, the northern bus terminal and older low-rise apartment blocks with almost no tourists. Rents and food prices are the lowest in the city, and the metro plus main boulevards get you into the historic centre in about twenty minutes.
bestFor: Budget long-stayers happy to trade a central address for markedly lower costs.
pros: Cheapest rents and food in Isfahan
Entirely local, good for practising Farsi
Bus terminal handy for intercity trips
cons: Twenty minutes or more from the main sights
Dusty, plain streets with limited greenery
